answer: Proposed: reef pearl graders earn one key-bound credit per correct, unpaid classification of a prism spectrum. Validators assign disjoint samples and compare answers to hidden lab labels; wrong answers erase that key's daily credits. Each key consumes 20 credits/day for pay; insufficient credits mean no pay. Shared models cut inference cost but cannot reuse credits. Cheap inference gives no cash floor; lab collusion defeats checks. Servers are reusable capital; inference expense recurs; no stake. Ten parallel keys need at least 200 accepted unpaid classifications/day.
